title: Trees
subtitle: Follow structure, specify answers, map and search, and count traversal work
description: Separate labels from structure; count leaves and map over trees as SICP does; justify aggregation, transformation and first-match search contracts; measure node visits and reuse completed answers.
estimateNote: Author estimate, not learner-measured: lesson 25–35 minutes (about 3,300 words with ten code blocks), lab 55–75 minutes (four functions written from stubs at 8–15 minutes each, one measurement, one mastery challenge). The SICP reading is optional reference and excluded.
sourceAttribution: Python lesson on SICP section 2.2.2 (Hierarchical Structures) by Harold Abelson and Gerald Jay Sussman with Julie Sussman: count-leaves, scale-tree, tree-map, fringe and deep-reverse are the book's examples and exercises, translated to Python. The labelled-tree interface (tree, label, branches, is_leaf) and the fib_tree example follow John DeNero's Composing Programs (CC BY-SA 3.0), the text of UC Berkeley CS 61A. Prose, figures and lab exercises are written for this course. Independent course; not endorsed by MIT or UC Berkeley.
